The issue is fixed: `![x\"x](x)` with smarty now renders `

`, the same as the unescaped version. Nothing is committed. **Cause:** a backslash escape is held as a placeholder during parsing, and the placeholder used to be swapped back to the real character *after* the HTML was written out. Characters restored that late were never HTML-escaped, so a raw `"` ended up inside the `alt`/`title` attribute. Smarty makes `"` and `'` escapable, which is why it showed up there. Without smarty the same thing happens with `\>`. **Fix:** a new `UnescapeTreeprocessor` in `markdown/treeprocessors.py` restores escaped characters in text and attribute values *before* the HTML is written, so they get escaped like everything else. Upstream Python-Markdown fixed this the same way. - A subagent first tried a regex over the final HTML string to find tags. I replaced it with this approach because it's fragile. - I left the old `UnescapePostprocessor` registered. With the fix it should only catch leftover placeholders, e.g. in HTML that third-party extensions stash. Removing it would break extensions that call `deregister('unescape')`. Anything left for it is still restored without HTML-escaping. **One visible change:** an escaped `\>` in normal text now renders as `>` where it used to be a raw `>`. Both are valid HTML. I updated the one expected-output file that depended on it, `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html`. **Tests:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py`: escaped `"` in an image alt and in a link title, `\'` in an alt, and `\"` in plain text. - Core tests for an escaped `>` in an image alt (`test_images.py`) and in a link title (`test_links.py`). - Four of the new tests fail on the old code and all pass with the fix. The other two, `\'` in an alt and `\"` in plain text, pass with or without it; they check that harmless cases still render as before. - The full suite, run with `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover tests`, has the same 8 failures as before my change (raw-HTML tests in `test_html_blocks` and `test_md_in_html`), and nothing new fails. - `pytest tests` on the whole directory stops before running anything, because it can't collect `test_md_in_html.py`. That happens without my change too, so I ran pytest on the affected files instead: 290 passed. - Escapes also render correctly with md_in_html, toc, footnotes and tables. **Docs:** a bug-fix note in `docs/change_log/release-3.4.md`, and the `unescape` postprocessor entry in `docs/extensions/api.md` now says the new tree processor restores most escapes and the postprocessor only handles leftovers.
